doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Medical career and returning seriously to music
summary: As OB-GYN department chair in Vermont he played around the edges, then took lessons and joined bands in retirement.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well you sound like as a young man you had a career goal in mind and you achieved that and you had a long career in the medical field.

Yes. And medicine is obviously demanding. I was the Department Chair of OB-GYN at the University of Vermont so that was demanding and so I really kind of fit in music very much around the edges. And unfortunately when I’d come up here to play at reunions it was very much, like you say, I’d play a couple of tunes and I’d say, “Man my chops are dying.” But people put up with me, which was good of them. But when I got ready to retire I had always hoped that I could get quite serious about the music and so that’s when I started the music lessons and I actually play in church brass groups and concert bands, and just Vermont bands in the park for the summer. It just helped my reading and just as a chance to play and hear other musicians, and that’s been fun, so I’ve been able to be very serious about it for the last three years.
